svg.text: stdx's regular expressions against libraries in Rust, Go and Zig, on AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor
The median of 10 jobs on AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor, the CPU model of 10 of 18 jobs, the most of any: runs
The bars share one logarithmic axis of stdx over Rust regex. The other libraries stand in the columns at the right.
A bar is the median of stdx over Rust regex:
|—| the interval of the median: the jobs' 2nd lowest to 2nd highest ratio, 98% confidence
the median of another CPU model's jobs: AMD EPYC 9V45 96-Core Processor (2), Intel(R) Xeon(R) 6975P-C (1), INTEL(R)
XEON(R) PLATINUM 8573C (2), AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor (2), Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8370C CPU @ 2.80GHz (1)

stdx compiles both programs and readies a searcher, Rust's crate runs Regex::new and Go regexp.Compile. A program compiles a pattern once
and searches with it many times.
a word that is not there
a word that ends in ing
a number before a unit, second text
a line's first word, second text
A row is ahead or behind where its interval lies above or below 1, and level where it holds 1 inside 5% of 1. A row whose interval holds 1
and reaches past 5% is unclear: its jobs do not settle it. A difference inside 5% is one this chart calls too small to matter, and the
counts still name its direction. A bar ahead or behind inside 5% is drawn lighter, and the shaded band on each panel is 5% of 1.
The columns at the right are stdx's speed over another library's, the median of the jobs. A library has no speed (—) on a pattern that it
refuses, where its answer is not Go regexp's, and where it has no such call.
stdx timed again, last in each round, differed from stdx by at most 12.4% in any job of any row.
On another CPU model, these rows fall on the other side of 1: a number (AMD EPYC 9V45 96-Core Processor, 1.15); a number (AMD EPYC 9V74
80-Core Processor, 1.016); a number (Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8370C CPU @ 2.80GHz, 1.05); a word between two words (Intel(R) Xeon(R)
6975P-C, 0.95); a number before a unit, second text (Intel(R) Xeon(R) 6975P-C, 0.93); a number before a unit, second text (INTEL(R)
